Jonas — quick tech notes from my side (so engineering can scope the probe):

Observations / clarifying questions
- Fanout model: when you say 1->3 consumers, do those consumers need the same real-time token stream or different partial outputs? That affects whether we can multiplex a single model stream or need three independent model instances.
- Multiplexing: Redwood supports multiplexing multiple logical streams over fewer physical model instances via prefix-aware routing, but there are tradeoffs around KV cache reuse and latency tail in high-concurrency bursts.
- Per-connection concurrency: please confirm typical RTT and client chunk assembly expectations. SSE keeps a persistent connection per user — scaling to 750 concurrent connections is straightforward on the networking layer but the model-side concurrency needs shaping (continuous batching).
- Warm cache behavior: do you have session affinity (reusing prior context) or mostly stateless prompts? Warm KV cache can reduce TTFT for follow-up messages significantly.

Suggested probe config
- Model variant: Llama-3x-8q (quantized baseline) and one fp16 variant for comparison.
- Sequence assumptions: average prompt ~120 tokens, expected generation ~180 tokens. If your payloads differ, let us know; we’ll size batch windows accordingly.
- Chunking: start with a 250ms cadence target; log emitted-chunk sizes and gaps.
- Telemetry we’ll collect: TTFT per-request, token emit latency, model-level queueing time, kernel-run durations, and per-connection network RTT.

Operational ask
- We’ll need a small sample of production traces (anonymized) or a traffic replay that mimics the fanout to ensure packetization and chunk cadence match reality.
- Recommend a dedicated staging pool for the probe to avoid noisy-neighbor effects.

—
